title: C520 — Left-hand exterior mirror connector
introduction:
An exterior mirror can carry quite an electrical committee: movement, lighting, heating, position sensing, folding and a blind-spot indicator all appear in this reference. I start with the connector identity, then use the cavity drawing to find a row and read its circuit description. The table is a directory of recorded functions, not proof that every feature is fitted to a particular car.

Keep the circuit identifier, color, gauge, function and terminal reference together. Motor movement and position sensing are different jobs: one describes moving the mirror, while the other describes information about its position. Repeated cavity entries cannot be assumed to operate together or to be interchangeable.

This guide explains the record without selecting wires, kits or probe locations. Access, physical viewing direction, live tests and replacement methods are outside its scope; gauge conventions and Size and Used codes are undefined here. The count discrepancy and unresolved repeated assignments need review before the record can determine an applicable connection. The metadata Pin Count differs from the cavity count shown by the drawing and both pigtail records; the source does not reconcile that difference.

edits.why: In the printed view, the lower-numbered column is on the left and the higher-numbered column is on the right; numbering increases downward. I follow the printed cavity label into the table rather than using row order, because some cavity labels occur more than once there. All drawn cavities have outlined circles, which do not establish installed equipment or electrical condition. The left-side projection and other housing features describe the visible shape; their operating functions and the physical viewing direction are not identified.

Read Function alongside Circuit Number and Color to distinguish motor commands, the common motor connection, lighting, heating, ground, position sensing, folding and the blind-spot indicator. Keep the motor-direction wording conditional on its stated positive-polarity condition; the common-motor description includes both sides. Preserve the positive and negative markers and the left-or-driver wording without converting them into power-application instructions. The protection description remains a fuse-or-circuit-breaker supply. Blank Qualifier cells do not explain the repeated assignments or establish which equipment configuration applies, and the rear-turn-lamp description remains unresolved within this mirror record.

The pigtail table contains separate repair-lead records. I read Number, Service Part and Engineering Shell as different identification fields, then keep each record's remaining details attached to it. A shared shell entry does not by itself settle which kit applies. The pigtail gauge is a property of the listed repair lead, not an instruction to substitute that gauge throughout the mirror wiring. This table supplies lookup information without teaching kit selection, splicing or installation.

originalAuthorHold: Pin Count is 16, but the drawing labels cavities 1–12 and both pigtail records specify 12 cavities. The evidence does not reconcile the count difference.

Cavities 3, 6, 10 and 12 each have different circuit assignments with blank Qualifier cells. The record does not establish whether these are equipment alternatives or erroneous assignments, so no applicable assignment is selected.

The exterior-mirror record assigns cavity 3 both CLS22 for TURN LAMP LEFT MIRROR + and CLS23 for TURN LAMP LEFT REAR. Whether the rear-lamp description is intentional, configuration-specific or incorrect requires review.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 45 primary units, three complete source pages and sole figure, and 3 edits. Count, repeated assignments and rear-turn-lamp label ambiguity retained for bounded identification reading only.
